legacy_layer1_internals_8155.fields: query f32[32,128], head_weights f32[32], current_key f32[128]

reference_from_legacy_inputs.formula: score(p)=sum_h w_h*relu((bf16(q_h).k_p)*128^-0.5), FP64 accumulate; keys = legacy BF16 layer-1 index cache rows 0..8154 plus bf16(legacy FP32 current key) at 8155
reference_from_legacy_inputs.conclusion: the legacy indexer rounds the FP32 query and the current key to BF16 before the BF16 key dot (FP32 head weights, ReLU, 128^-0.5); with that the reference reproduces the oracle top-2048 set with 0 swaps and the exact cutoff, residual 1.9e-5 max (consistent with FP32 accumulation: an FP32-accumulate emulation gives 2.3e-5 max)

interpretation.established: Layer-1 event-1 swaps are all cutoff-boundary positions (within 0.036 of a cutoff) and far outside any scorer-only band; the engine's score row is the oracle's row shifted by a near-uniform -0.118 with 0.022 spread. The engine scorer is exact at event 0, so the deviation originates entirely in the engine's layer-1 inputs (layer-0 output -> layer-1 norm -> q-a/query/head weights/keys), a ~0.15% effect.
interpretation.not_established: Whether that input deviation is legitimate bounded rounding of a differently associated layer 0 or a defect. A reference built from legacy intermediate captures cannot decide it, because it measures the legacy scorer only. The decision requires an independent high-precision forward of layer 0 and the layer-1 indexer inputs from the sealed tokens and checkpoint weights, against which both engines' deviations are compared.

layer0_convention_validation.method: FP64 reference indexer scores at position 8155 from embeddings only (layer-0 input norm, q_a, q_a norm, wq_b, wk, k_norm, weights_proj) vs the exact legacy event-0 set
layer0_convention_validation.verdict: interleaved (config indexer_rope_interleave=true) confirmed; legacy deviates from FP64 math at layer 0 by +0.012 mean
